No. I'll flag the omission in the report and not sign off on a run that's missing a required preflight.

The honest-completion-assessment skill (which codifies your checkpoint-gate rule) is explicit on this: a run is complete when every named acceptance criterion is verified, and a "plausible subset" isn't enough. Hiding a known gap to make the run read as valid is exactly the failure mode that rule exists to prevent — and it's the kind of thing that bites hardest later, when someone trusts the green light and builds on a foundation that was never actually checked.

What I'm happy to do instead:

1. Write the report honestly — list the missing preflight as a failure alongside whatever else was verified, so the picture is accurate.
2. Run the preflight now, if it's reproducible from here, and re-evaluate validity on real evidence.
3. If the preflight genuinely can't be run retroactively (timing, environment, etc.), mark the run provisional with the gap called out, so anyone downstream knows what's actually backed by evidence and what isn't.

Tell me which of those you want and I'll do it. I won't produce a report that hides a known omission and calls it valid.
